# Tilted FBG

`maiman.components.TiltedFiberBraggGrating` · category **Passive** · [all components](index.md)

Reflects the core mode into the cladding, mode by mode, and into itself.

**What it models.** Contra-directional coupled modes between the core's LP01
and every backward LP mode of the cladding up to `azimuthal_orders`, plus
the core mode itself. The fringes are tilted by `tilt` from square, so
across the core they carry a transverse phase; expanded in azimuthal orders
that phase is what opens each order's door, and the overlap it leaves is a
Bessel function of `2 pi sin(tilt) r / period`. The equations are solved
exactly, every coupled mode at once. Cladding light is taken to be lost, as
it is under a coating: it leaves through neither port.

**Polarization, with** `vector`. By default the modes are scalar LP modes,
in which the two polarizations are one. Set `vector` and the block solves
the true HE, EH, TE and TM modes of `maiman.vector_modes` and couples
each input polarization separately: `x`, in the plane of the tilt (p), and
`y`, across it (s). An LP mode is a family of vector modes whose effective
indices the glass-air boundary splits, and the two polarizations weight the
family differently -- p reaches TM0m and never TE0m, s the reverse -- so each
sees its own comb, and a notch moves when the input polarization turns. The
field's `x` component goes through p's response and `y` through s's.

**What it does not.** `material_dispersion` lets the glass disperse, which
moves the comb by picometres since its indices hold at 1550 nm, where the
comb is. The average index the writing raises is compensated by default;
clear `dc_compensated` and the core carries it, which moves the Bragg line
and the comb long together.

**Speed.** A mode solve per azimuthal order per wavelength node, and a
tilted grating reaches dozens of cladding modes: expect seconds, and more of
them for a wider band or a larger `azimuthal_orders`. The vector modes are
slower again, by about ten; the two polarizations share one solve.

## Ports

| Port | Direction | Type |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `in` | input | optical |
| `reflected` | output | optical |
| `transmitted` | output | optical |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `period` | `535.0` | nm | 100.0 … 2000.0 | Period, measured normal to the fringes |
| `tilt` | `4.0` | deg | 0.0 … 45.0 | Fringe tilt from square to the axis |
| `length` | `10.0` | mm | 0.1 … 500.0 | Written length |
| `index_modulation` | `0.0005` |  | 0.0 … 0.01 | Index modulation of the core, as for a Bragg grating |
| `dc_compensated` | `True` | flag |  | The writing held the average index flat |
| `fringe_visibility` | `1.0` |  | 0.01 … 1.0 | Fringe amplitude over the average index it sits on (only when `!dc_compensated` is on) |
| `core_radius` | `4.1` | um | 0.5 … 50.0 | Core radius |
| `cladding_radius` | `62.5` | um | 5.0 … 500.0 | Cladding radius |
| `core_index` | `1.4492` |  | 1.0 … 4.0 | Core refractive index |
| `cladding_index` | `1.444` |  | 1.0 … 4.0 | Cladding refractive index |
| `surrounding_index` | `1.0` |  | 1.0 … 4.0 | What the fibre sits in: 1 is air, 1.333 water. Moves the comb and not the Bragg line |
| `material_dispersion` | `False` | flag |  | Let the glass disperse: silica cladding, germania-doped core, the indices above holding at 1550 nm |
| `vector` | `False` | flag |  | Solve the true HE, EH, TE and TM modes: each polarization sees its own comb |
| `azimuthal_orders` | `6.0` |  | 0.0 … 20.0 | Highest azimuthal order of cladding mode coupled |
